children.text: A nonrelativistic particle of mass \(m\) moves without friction in the horizontal xy-plane. Across \(x=x_1\), potential changes from zero in region I to \(V_0\) in region II. It leaves \(O=(0,0)\) at speed \(v_1\), angle \(\theta_1\) to the x-axis, crosses at \((x_1,\alpha)\), then reaches \(P=(x_0,y_0)\) at speed \(v_2\), angle \(\theta_2\). Its fixed-energy action is \(\mathcal A=m\int v(s)\,ds\), stationary on the physical path. Ignore gravity and relativistic effects in every part. Use \(h=6.63\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\,s}\), \(m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(e=1.60\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\).

children.text: Two optical media have refractive indices \(n_1,n_2\), separated by a horizontal line. Ray angles \(i_1,i_2\) are measured from the y-axis. Derive their relation from stationary travel time.
A laser enters horizontally at \(y=0\) into sugar solution with index \(n(y)\), which decreases upwards. Let \(n_0=n(0)\). Find the downward beam slope.
For \(n(y)=n_0-ky\), \(k>0\), derive \(x(y)\) with \(x(0)=0\). The tank bottom is \(y=-y_0\).
Relate phase change \(\Delta\varphi\) of a de Broglie wave to action change \(\Delta\mathcal A\).
A small opening CD of width \(d\ll x_1,x_0-x_1\) is placed at the interface. Path OCP is classical. Find the first-order phase difference of OCP and ODP.

children.text: An electron beam travels through a narrow slit F and point P with OFP a straight line at \(\theta=10.0000^\circ\). Speeds are \(v_1=2.0000\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}\), \(v_2=1.9900\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}\). The screen is \(x_0-x_1=250.00\,\mathrm{mm}\) beyond the slit. Find the voltage accelerating electrons from rest to \(v_1\).
A second slit G lies 215.00 nm below F. If the phase difference at P is \(2\pi\beta\), find \(\beta\).
Find the smallest distance from P to a point of zero detection on the screen, and state its direction.
The beam cross-section is \(500\,\mathrm{nm}\times500\,\mathrm{nm}\), and apparatus length is 2 m. Find the minimum number flux for at least one electron on average in the setup.

statement.text:
The Extremum Principle
A nonrelativistic particle of mass \(m\) moves without friction in the horizontal xy-plane. Across \(x=x_1\), potential changes from zero in region I to \(V_0\) in region II. It leaves \(O=(0,0)\) at speed \(v_1\), angle \(\theta_1\) to the x-axis, crosses at \((x_1,\alpha)\), then reaches \(P=(x_0,y_0)\) at speed \(v_2\), angle \(\theta_2\). Its fixed-energy action is \(\mathcal A=m\int v(s)\,ds\), stationary on the physical path. Ignore gravity and relativistic effects in every part. Use \(h=6.63\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\,s}\), \(m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(e=1.60\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\).

A1. Energy across the step
Find the speed in region II from energy conservation.
A2. Tangential momentum
Relate speeds to the two trajectory angles.
A3. Stationary action
Write \(\mathcal A(\alpha)\), then use stationarity to relate \(v_1/v_2\) to the coordinates.
B1. Fermat and refraction

Two optical media have refractive indices \(n_1,n_2\), separated by a horizontal line. Ray angles \(i_1,i_2\) are measured from the y-axis. Derive their relation from stationary travel time.
B2. Graded-index beam slope
A laser enters horizontally at \(y=0\) into sugar solution with index \(n(y)\), which decreases upwards. Let \(n_0=n(0)\). Find the downward beam slope.
B3. Beam trajectory
For \(n(y)=n_0-ky\), \(k>0\), derive \(x(y)\) with \(x(0)=0\). The tank bottom is \(y=-y_0\).
B4. Bottom intersection
Find \(x_0\) for \(y_0=10.0\,\mathrm{cm}\), \(n_0=1.50\), \(k=0.050\,\mathrm{cm^{-1}}\).
C1. Wave phase and action
Relate phase change \(\Delta\varphi\) of a de Broglie wave to action change \(\Delta\mathcal A\).
C2. First-order phase difference
A small opening CD of width \(d\ll x_1,x_0-x_1\) is placed at the interface. Path OCP is classical. Find the first-order phase difference of OCP and ODP.
D1. Electron accelerating voltage

An electron beam travels through a narrow slit F and point P with OFP a straight line at \(\theta=10.0000^\circ\). Speeds are \(v_1=2.0000\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}\), \(v_2=1.9900\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}\). The screen is \(x_0-x_1=250.00\,\mathrm{mm}\) beyond the slit. Find the voltage accelerating electrons from rest to \(v_1\).
D2. Two-slit phase
A second slit G lies 215.00 nm below F. If the phase difference at P is \(2\pi\beta\), find \(\beta\).
D3. Nearest interference minimum
Find the smallest distance from P to a point of zero detection on the screen, and state its direction.
D4. Minimum electron flux
The beam cross-section is \(500\,\mathrm{nm}\times500\,\mathrm{nm}\), and apparatus length is 2 m. Find the minimum number flux for at least one electron on average in the setup.

children.text: \(mv_1^2/2=mv_2^2/2+V_0\), so \(v_2=\sqrt{v_1^2-2V_0/m}\), provided the trajectory can enter region II.
The potential force is normal to the boundary, so \(mv_1\sin\theta_1=mv_2\sin\theta_2\). Thus \(v_2=v_1\sin\theta_1/\sin\theta_2\).

\[\mathcal A=m v_1\sqrt{x_1^2+\alpha^2}+m v_2\sqrt{(x_0-x_1)^2+(y_0-\alpha)^2}.\] Setting its derivative to zero gives \[\frac{v_1\alpha}{\sqrt{x_1^2+\alpha^2}}=\frac{v_2(y_0-\alpha)}{\sqrt{(x_0-x_1)^2+(y_0-\alpha)^2}},\] which is the tangential-momentum relation.
The travel time is \(t=(n_1l_1+n_2l_2)/c\). Vary the crossing point along the interface. Its derivative vanishes when \(n_1\sin i_1=n_2\sin i_2\), Snell's law.
Across horizontal layers, \(n\sin i=n_0\). Since \(dy/dx=-\cot i\), \[\frac{dy}{dx}=-\sqrt{n(y)^2/n_0^2-1}.\]
\[\Delta\varphi_{CD}=\frac{2\pi md}{h}(v_1\sin\theta_1-v_2\sin\theta_2)=0.\] Stationary action means neighbouring paths interfere constructively to first order.
The incident and outgoing path differences subtract: \[\beta=\frac{m_ed}{h}(v_1-v_2)\sin\theta=5.13.\]

The nearest half-integer phase is \(5.5\times2\pi\). For outgoing angle \(\theta+\Delta\theta\), \(m_ed[v_1\sin\theta-v_2\sin(\theta+\Delta\theta)]/h=5.5\). Linearizing sine gives \(\Delta\theta\simeq-6.3\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{rad}\). Thus \(\Delta y=(x_0-x_1)\sec^2\theta\,\Delta\theta\simeq-16.2\,\mathrm{\mu m}\), below P.
Mean occupancy is \(N=IA\ell/v\). Set \(N=1\) and use \(v\simeq2\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}\): \(I_{min}=v/(A\ell)=4\times10^{19}\,\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}\).

solution.text:
The Extremum Principle
A1. Energy across the step
\(mv_1^2/2=mv_2^2/2+V_0\), so \(v_2=\sqrt{v_1^2-2V_0/m}\), provided the trajectory can enter region II.
A2. Tangential momentum
The potential force is normal to the boundary, so \(mv_1\sin\theta_1=mv_2\sin\theta_2\). Thus \(v_2=v_1\sin\theta_1/\sin\theta_2\).
A3. Stationary action
\[\mathcal A=m v_1\sqrt{x_1^2+\alpha^2}+m v_2\sqrt{(x_0-x_1)^2+(y_0-\alpha)^2}.\] Setting its derivative to zero gives \[\frac{v_1\alpha}{\sqrt{x_1^2+\alpha^2}}=\frac{v_2(y_0-\alpha)}{\sqrt{(x_0-x_1)^2+(y_0-\alpha)^2}},\] which is the tangential-momentum relation.
B1. Fermat and refraction
The travel time is \(t=(n_1l_1+n_2l_2)/c\). Vary the crossing point along the interface. Its derivative vanishes when \(n_1\sin i_1=n_2\sin i_2\), Snell's law.
B2. Graded-index beam slope
Across horizontal layers, \(n\sin i=n_0\). Since \(dy/dx=-\cot i\), \[\frac{dy}{dx}=-\sqrt{n(y)^2/n_0^2-1}.\]
B3. Beam trajectory
Integrate \(dx/dy=-n_0/\sqrt{(n_0-ky)^2-n_0^2}\). Using \(\int du/\sqrt{u^2-1}=\ln(u+\sqrt{u^2-1})\), \[x(y)=\frac{n_0}{k}\ln\left(1-\frac{ky}{n_0}+\sqrt{(1-ky/n_0)^2-1}\right).\]
B4. Bottom intersection
Substitute \(y=-10.0\,\mathrm{cm}\) in B3: \(x_0=30\ln[(4+\sqrt7)/3]=23.9\,\mathrm{cm}\).
C1. Wave phase and action
\(d\varphi=2\pi ds/\lambda=2\pi mv\,ds/h\), so \(\Delta\varphi=2\pi\Delta\mathcal A/h\).
C2. First-order phase difference
\[\Delta\varphi_{CD}=\frac{2\pi md}{h}(v_1\sin\theta_1-v_2\sin\theta_2)=0.\] Stationary action means neighbouring paths interfere constructively to first order.
D1. Electron accelerating voltage
Nonrelativistically \(eU_1=m_ev_1^2/2\), giving \(U_1=1.139\times10^3\,\mathrm V\).
D2. Two-slit phase
The incident and outgoing path differences subtract: \[\beta=\frac{m_ed}{h}(v_1-v_2)\sin\theta=5.13.\]
D3. Nearest interference minimum
The nearest half-integer phase is \(5.5\times2\pi\). For outgoing angle \(\theta+\Delta\theta\), \(m_ed[v_1\sin\theta-v_2\sin(\theta+\Delta\theta)]/h=5.5\). Linearizing sine gives \(\Delta\theta\simeq-6.3\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{rad}\). Thus \(\Delta y=(x_0-x_1)\sec^2\theta\,\Delta\theta\simeq-16.2\,\mathrm{\mu m}\), below P.
D4. Minimum electron flux
Mean occupancy is \(N=IA\ell/v\). Set \(N=1\) and use \(v\simeq2\times10^7\,\mathrm{m/s}\): \(I_{min}=v/(A\ell)=4\times10^{19}\,\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}\).
